correctness.rationale: For every t>-1, compute complete monomial norms exactly by beta integral and reconstruct the kernel from its orthogonal basis. The binomial identity proves the closed form, with normalization K(0)=(t+1)(t+2)/(2pi). The Cayley ratio maps the open disk to the right half-plane, bounding the principal argument and proving the strict index inequality 1<=j<(t+2)/4. Exact solving yields every negative real root, and differentiation proves simple roots. Finite numerical tests verify representative coefficients and root locations but are not the all-parameter proof. The t=2 and t=6 boundary cases correctly exclude s=-1.

value.rationale: Euclidean boundary-distance powers are a canonical naturally parameterized Bergman family in current analytic-dependence research. Their sharp zero-free range, explicit complete zero set, phase transitions every four exponent units, and negative-ray rigidity are structurally motivated new information. They contrast with the ordinarily studied standard (1-|z|^2)^t weights, whose Bergman kernels never vanish. Exact natural classifications qualify independently of downstream theorems.
